issues.legal_issue: An accepted offer and related correspondence that contemplate a later lease, but create no present demise, constitute an agreement to lease rather than a lease chargeable with stamp duty.
material_facts: The offer to take the plot was made with the company expressly identifying itself as a promoter that would construct flats and transfer the relevant rights to a cooperative society formed by purchasers.
The government accepted the tender knowing the company’s stated role as promoter.

The invitation contemplated execution of a separate agreement to lease before possession, and the draft stated that no legal interest in the land would arise until a lease was executed and registered.
No present demise occurred when the tender was accepted; possession was later described as deemed possession.
The stamp authority treated the correspondence as a lease and demanded stamp duty.
issues.conclusion: The correspondence constituted only an agreement to lease, not a lease or an instrument chargeable to stamp duty, so the stamp-duty demand could not stand.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 2(7) of the Registration Act, an agreement to lease is included as a lease only when it effects an actual, present demise. An executory agreement that merely binds the parties to grant and accept a lease in the future does not create that demise. The Court relied on Tiruvenibai v. Lilabai, which applied Hemanta Kumari Debi v. Midnapur Zamindari Co. Ltd., and discussed the distinction between a lease and an agreement for lease in Woodfall, Hill and Redman, and Green v. Bowes-Lyon. Since the correspondence was not a lease, it did not fall within section 2(n) of the Bombay Stamp Act, 1958 as an instrument chargeable with duty under Article 36.

predicates.stamp_duty_challenge: A party challenges a demand for stamp duty imposed on correspondence said to create a lease.
predicates.separate_lease_contemplated: The parties contemplated executing a separate lease document later.
predicates.no_present_demise: The accepted offer and correspondence did not immediately create a demise or a present legal interest in the land.

issues.definition: When a stamp-duty challenge concerns correspondence that contemplates a later lease and creates no present demise, the demand is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: The benefit of an executory agreement to lease may be assigned to the cooperative society intended to receive the land rights when the promoter’s role and that intended transfer were disclosed to and accepted by the government.
material_facts: The company’s offer and accompanying information stated that it acted as promoter and that purchasers would form a cooperative society to which the company’s rights, including the right to a lease, would be transferred.
The government sanctioned the lease in the company’s favour as promoter of a cooperative housing society.
After the society was formed, the government sanctioned the request to transfer the rights, title and interest in the plot to it.
Although the invitation restricted transfer without government consent, the government approved the transfer and the restriction was not enforced.
issues.conclusion: The benefit of the agreement to lease was assignable to the cooperative society, and the government’s approved transfer supported execution of the lease in the society’s favour.
issues.legal_principle: The benefit of an executory agreement to lease can be assigned. The Court treated the disclosed promoter arrangement, the government’s acceptance of that arrangement, and its later sanction of the transfer as establishing that the company assigned the benefit of the agreement to the cooperative society. It also accepted that the restriction on transfer had not been enforced in the circumstances.

rule.if: lease_assignment_dispute and promoter_role_disclosed and society_intended_recipient and government_approved_transfer

predicates.lease_assignment_dispute: A dispute concerns whether the benefit of an agreement to lease may pass from a promoter to a cooperative society.
predicates.promoter_role_disclosed: The promoter disclosed that it was acting as a promoter and that the land rights would be transferred to a society formed by the purchasers.
predicates.society_intended_recipient: The society formed by the purchasers was identified as the intended recipient of the land rights.
predicates.government_approved_transfer: The government approved the transfer of the relevant rights in the plot to the society.

issues.definition: When an assignment dispute involves a disclosed promoter arrangement, an identified society as recipient, and government approval of the transfer, the agreement’s benefit is assignable to the society.
